answer: Each agent may propose work, but payment depends on a bond locked in a shared ledger and forfeited if independent reviewers reject the result. Reviewers are sampled from agents with a history of accepted work, and their own bonds are slashed for colluding or careless approval. A sybil can mint identities cheaply, but cannot cheaply multiply bonded stake or credible review histories; it must risk real capital and spend time earning trust. Even a saffron label or a hollow profile cannot bridge that gap.
